React Compiler only optimizes code that follows the rules of React. A compiler that can't check hooks and memoization dependencies itself doesn't trust a component or a hook with a comment that turns off `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` or `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`, and skips the whole function. This rule is for those comments.

`bun lint` runs the compiler with both of those checks on, and then the compiler doesn't look for the comments. So this rule reports nothing, with any config. It exists because `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` has it and oxlint has it as `react/rule-suppression`, and a config that names it needs to keep working.

A function with such a comment is checked like every other function, so the other React Compiler rules still report in it.

{/* never reports */}

## Examples

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import { useEffect } from "react";

function Title({ text }) {
  useEffect(() => {
    document.title = text;
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);
  return <h1>{text}</h1>;
}
```

Not reported with an oxlint config either:

{/* good {"config": "oxlint"} */}
```jsx
import { useEffect } from "react";

function Title({ text }) {
  useEffect(() => {
    document.title = text;
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);
  return <h1>{text}</h1>;
}
```

An `eslint-disable` or `oxlint-disable` comment for the whole file, and oxlint's names `react/rules-of-hooks` and `react/exhaustive-deps`, make no difference:

{/* good {"config": "oxlint"} */}
```jsx
/* oxlint-disable react/rules-of-hooks */
import { useState } from "react";

function Counter({ isEnabled }) {
  if (!isEnabled) return null;
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>{count}</button>;
}
```
